Fastest and most reliable path for coding. Plug the ENET cable into the OBD port and the phone (USB-C Ethernet adapter), or join the ENET-WiFi adapter\u2019s network, switch the ignition on, then tap Find car. A 2012 F10 gateway speaks HSFZ on port 6801.

ELM327/STN-based dongles (vLinker, OBDLink, UniCarScan, generic ELM327 v1.5). The app speaks BMW\u2019s extended-addressed UDS on the D-CAN bus, so coding and diagnostics both work. Slower than ENET; an STN-chip adapter is recommended for coding writes.
Tip: keep the ignition on (engine off) for coding, and connect a battery charger for long sessions. The app backs up each coding block before writing and verifies every write by reading it back.

Before you connect to a car

This app writes configuration bytes to your car’s control modules.

The coding definitions bundled with the app are illustrative and are marked unverified. Unverified maps can be exercised freely in demo mode, and the app refuses to write them to real hardware. To code a real car you must supply maps verified against your own car’s coding data.

Reading fault codes and live data is passive. Clearing fault codes is reversible.

You are responsible for what you change. Keep the battery charged, keep the ignition on, and never code while driving. This software comes with no warranty, and it is not affiliated with or endorsed by any vehicle manufacturer.
